articles.summary: El hispano-montenegrino estuvo tan errático en su regreso al Palau (10 puntos con 1/7 triples) como todo su equipo (7/31 t3)
articles.body: Mirotic había salido victorioso en sus tres visitas anteriores al Palau (dos con el Armani y una con el Monaco) desde que fue despedido por la puerta de atrás por el Barça, pero a la cuarta fue vencido (89-86). No hubo venganza del ex, tan errático (10 puntos con 1/7 triples) como todo su equipo (7/31 t3). Y encima falló el triple para forzar la prórroga. TJ Shorts, el pequeño diablo taronja, hizo lo que pudo (19+4 asistencias), pero no bastó ante el juego colectivo de los azulgranas, que con su gran intensidad defensiva lograron secar el habitualmente prolífico ataque del Valencia. Y en ataque tuvo muchos focos para hacer daño con Punter (13), Nebo (12+4), Robinson (12) y Martin (10) muy activos. El inicio del partido fue un quiero y no puedo del Barcelona, voluntarioso en defensa pero con poca fluidez ofensiva ante un Valencia jugando casi de memoria y que cogió las primeras ventajas en el primer cuarto con el acierto de Shorts y el suplente Mirotic pese a su flojo 1/7 en triples (19-26, min 10). El escurridizo Shorts puso la máxima para los taronjas (19-28, min 21) antes de que el Barça entrase en combustión propulsado por los triples de Parra, Martin y Punter con un parcial de 15-2 (34-30, min 16). Mirotic, Rivero y Brooks, con un triple sobre la bocina, devolvieron el mando al Valencia (39-40, min 20), que sobrevivía a su 2/13 desde el triple. En la reanudación salió el Barça más esforzado en defensa y más atinado en ataque para demarrar con un parcial de 10-1 (49-41, min 23). Un triple de Brooks no logró detener la sangría (55-44, min 25). Moore y Shorts intentaron en vano solventar el atasco taronja (64-51. min 29). Más éxito tuvieron Rivero, Brooks, Puerto y Shorts (68-60, min 30). El inicio del último acto fue una locura, con Punter, Robinson y Martin poniendo el contrapunto a un Shorts desatado (75-64). Los triples de Reuvers y Brooks y las embestidas de Sako y Moore hicieron soñar al Valencia (79-76, min 37). Osetkowski contestó con un triple a un 2+1 de Balcerowski (82-79). Mirotic neutralizó un tiro libre de Punter (83-81, a 1.30). Nebo anotó dos tiros libres y Shorts otros dos. Fue Parra con un triple quien dio el estirón definitivo (88-83). Mirotic y Taylor acercaron al Valencia a 13 segundos (88-86). Pero el hispano-montenegrino erró el triple sobre la bocina para forzar la prórroga. No hubo venganza del ex. 89 - Barça (19+20+29+21): Robinson (12), Martin (10), Punter (13), Parra (8) y Balcerowski (9), -cinco inicial-, Gibson (1), Brizuela (4), Ubal (7), Nkamhoua (6), Nuñez (-), Evbuomwan (7), Nebo (12). 86 - Valencia Basket (26+14+20+26): TJ Shorts (19), Brooks (11), Taylor (4), Osetkowski (3) y Sako (6), -cinco inicial-, Puerto (5), Reuvers (8), Saint-Supery (-), Cárdenas (4), Moore (9), Mirotic (10), Rivero (7). Árbitros: Carlos Peruga, Alberto Baena y Andrés Fernández. Sin eliminados. articles.title: Caitlin Clark opens up about her next move after Fever's heartbreaking playoff elimination
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark is already looking beyond the Indiana Fever's disappointing playoff exit.
articles.body: Caitlin Clark is already looking beyond the Indiana Fever's disappointing playoff exit. After a season that ended with a first-round loss to the Las Vegas Aces, the 24-year-old guard has outlined what she wants to improve before returning to the WNBA in 2027. Her focus goes beyond scoring and records. Clark wants to become a stronger leader, build closer relationships with younger teammates and help Indiana attract and retain key talent. With major offseason decisions ahead, her latest comments offer a glimpse into how she hopes to shape the Fever's next chapter.Caitlin Clark reveals her leadership goals after third WNBA seasonClark discussed her development during a media session on Thursday, reflecting on how life as a professional athlete has changed her. Moving to a new city and adjusting to life away from home have helped her grow, but she believes there is still room to improve.“I think when you become a professional, it makes you grow up a little bit,” Clark said at the 10:16 mark. “At the same time, I’m only 24, but I feel like you live on your own, you’re in a new city, and you try to figure everything out. I feel very comfortable living here, and I love the people in this city. I love the way they support basketball, I love the way they support women’s basketball, I love getting to play here.“I think for myself, just continuing to improve (in) a lot of different ways going into my fourth year. I think just like leadership and my voice, those are some of the biggest areas I can continue to improve as our point guard.”Her comments point to a clear priority for the upcoming offseason. As Indiana's point guard, Clark must help guide the team on the court while building trust with the players around her.The Fever finished the 2026 regular season with a 28-16 record and secured the sixth seed in the playoffs. Despite a strong campaign, they could not get past the defending champions, the Aces, in their first-round series.Caitlin Clark outlines Indiana Fever offseason plansClark also wants to play a more active role in helping Indiana's younger players develop. Rather than leaving team chemistry to training camp, she hopes to spend time working alongside them during the offseason.“Going into the offseason, getting free agents to come here,” she continued. “Obviously, retaining Kelsey (Mitchell).“I think also going into the offseason, I want to make a point to be able to get out and work out with a lot of our young players. Whether that’s Raven (Johnson), whether that’s [Makayla Timpson]. Just to be in the gym and to just continue to develop that bond and chemistry of playing with them.”Retaining Kelsey Mitchell and attracting free agents could be important as Indiana looks to strengthen its roster. Clark's willingness to invest time in younger teammates also suggests she wants to contribute beyond her individual performances.The guard set several WNBA and franchise records during the season, but the Fever fell short of their championship ambitions. Now, the challenge is turning individual success into a deeper playoff run.Clark's fourth professional season will bring fresh expectations. articles.title: Dream must play WNBA Finals home games at smaller Gateway Center Arena, rather than State Farm Arena in downtown Atlanta
articles.summary: State Farm Arena already has events booked for the dates of Games 3, 4 and 6 of the WNBA Finals.
articles.body:
After playing three home playoff games at State Farm Arena during their run to the WNBA Finals, the Atlanta Dream will have to host games for the league's championship series at the smaller Gateway Center Arena.

The Dream played six of their 22 home games during the regular season at the larger State Farm Arena, home to the NBA's Atlanta Hawks. With a capacity of 16,888 for basketball games, the larger facility could accommodate what were certain to be bigger crowds for two WNBA Finals games.

Additionally, State Farm Arena is located in downtown Atlanta, presumably providing easier access from hotels, highways and mass transit, in addition to more parking and ability to walk to the stadium from the city center.

Instead, the Dream will have to play at the smaller Gateway Center Arena, which seats 3,500 for basketball games and is located just outside Atlanta in College Park, Georgia.

By comparison, the Golden State Valkyries will host Games 1, 2, 5 and 7 at Chase Center in San Francisco, also the home of the NBA's Golden State Warriors, which seats 18,064 for basketball .

The Dream have attempted to move their WNBA Finals games to a larger arena in the area, but have thus far been unsuccessful in those discussions, according to USA Today's Meghan L. Hall .

Among the other possible venues in the Atlanta metropolitan area are McCavish Pavilion on the campus of Georgia Tech, which can seat 8,600 for basketball games. The Convocation Center at Georgia State University also has a capacity of 7,500 for basketball. Gas South Arena in Duluth, Georgia — located nearly 30 miles from downtown Atlanta — can accommodate 12,750 and was also considered.

State Farm Arena is unavailable for Games 3, 4 and 6 of the WNBA Finals — scheduled for Oct. 22, Oct. 24 and Oct. 29, respectively — with a concert by Sombr and two Hawks regular-season games , including the team's home opener, already booked at the venue.

"We didn't have playoff games [at State Farm Arena] last year... but we had a couple of games there, and they felt like playoff games," Dream guard Rhyne Howard told USA Today . "So I think for us to have had those during the season and have the outcome that we had, I think it helps us get ready for this environment."

Last week, the Dream announced that they will play all of their 2027 home games at State Farm Arena . Each team will have 25 home games as part of an expanded 50-game WNBA regular-season schedule. However, that obviously does nothing to solve the problem of what to do during the WNBA Finals.

articles.title: New 76ers Rumors on Roster After Hukporti's Season-Ending Injury Amid Buzz on LeBron James' Role
articles.summary: The Philadelphia 76ers don't have much depth at center behind star big man Joel Embiid after Ariel Hukporti suffered a season-ending Achilles tear, and they don't currently have many avenues to address the concern.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia 76ers don't have much depth at center behind star big man Joel Embiid after Ariel Hukporti suffered a season-ending Achilles tear, and they don't currently have many avenues to address the concern.

According to NBA insiders Marc Stein and Jake Fischer , "Even before losing Hukporti, Philadelphia knew it was limited by first apron concerns in making any meaningful roster alterations beyond filling its third two-way spot. Sources say that the Sixers are unlikely to add a big man on a standard NBA deal before early December, when a pro-rated minimum salary would no longer take the team's payroll past the first apron threshold. The only apparent pathway to bringing in a replacement sooner is swinging a trade that actually reduces the team's overall salary commitments by roughly $600,000."

One option could be trading a player like forward Jabari Walker, though he's looked very good during the preseason. Another option may be playing small when Embiid sits, with players like Dean Wade, Dominick Barlow or perhaps even LeBron James operating as a small-ball center.

It isn't the ideal situation—especially considering Embiid's injury history—but the Sixers don't have much flexibility to explore alternate plans, at least until December.

articles.title: New Knicks Rumors on Karl-Anthony Towns and Josh Hart Contract Talks, Deuce McBride Trade Buzz
articles.summary: With the NBA season just over a week away, the focus around the New York Knicks has been less about their title defense and more about contract talks with their stars.
articles.body:
With the NBA season just over a week away, the focus around the New York Knicks has been less about their title defense and more about contract talks with their stars.

Amid talks with Karl-Anthony Towns and Josh Hart, the Knicks announced that they're pausing all contract negotiations until later in the season.

That, of course, affects Towns and Hart, and NBA insiders Marc Stein and Jake Fischer noted it also impacts Deuce McBride and Tyler Kolek, both of whom are on the final years of their respective deals.

According to Stein and Fischer, "Towns was the only member of that foursome whose camp had been seriously engaged by the Knicks at the time of Friday's statement."

The two insiders added that the Knicks have "prioritized talks with Towns over Hart to this point."

Hart has a $22.4 million team option next year, so it remains to be seen whether he'll enter free agency. Both he and Towns posted messages on social media that should encourage the fan base.

While it would be a bit surprising to see either Towns or Hart be traded this season, the same can't be said for McBride. Stein and Fischer reported that rival teams have described him as "a likely trade candidate as the season unfolds given the uncertainty surrounding his own Knicks future."

McBride was a solid role player on a championship team last year, and his affordable, expiring contract will certainly interest contenders as the trade deadline nears.

articles.summary: Charlotte Hornets forward Brandon Miller could be the next young player in line for a very lucrative extension.
articles.body:
Charlotte Hornets forward Brandon Miller could be the next young player in line for a very lucrative extension.

According to NBA insiders Marc Stein and Jake Fischer , "Miller is still projected by various league observers to ultimately come to terms with the Hornets on an extension that could exceed Amen Thompson's new five-year, $200 million deal with the Rockets. In conversations with front office executives around the NBA this week, there seemed to be a growing consensus among rival decision-makers that Miller's deal has the potential to be richer in a nod to his higher offensive ceiling."

That comes after Brandin Podziemski signed a five-year, $110 million rookie-scale contract extension with the Golden State Warriors on Saturday.

Miller, 23, averaged 20.2 points, 4.9 rebounds and 3.3 assists in 65 games last season, shooting 38.3 percent from three. With LaMelo Bell now in Minnesota, Miller's very much the face of the Hornets alongside Kon Knueppel.

Meanwhile, Stein and Fischer reported that Cason Wallace and the Oklahoma City Thunder are negotiating an extension worth around $25 million per recent season, though there are questions around the NBA whether the deal could exceed that AAV.

Wallace, 22, averaged 8.6 points, 3.1 rebounds, 2.6 assists and 1.9 steals per game last season, shooting 35.1 percent from three. His defensive impact makes him very valuable to the Thunder as they seek another title.

The No. 4 overall pick out of North Carolina continued to show out in preseason, putting together a strong performance in a 133-128 loss to the Denver Nuggets on Sunday.

He put up 15 points in his first preseason game before dropping 17 against the Memphis Grizzlies on Friday, and those numbers are not to be overlooked, especially from a player going up against NBA players for the first time ever.

At 6'9", Wilson has the height and wingspan to defend every position and make an impact around the rim on offense, but still possesses the athleticism and shotmaking ability to score from outside the paint.

Once the rookie gets comfortable, it won't be a surprise if he has a strong case for the Rookie of the Year award at the end of the season.

articles.title: ‘Magnet Ball 2.0,’ ‘Not Even Trying To Hide It’ — NBA Fans Raise Red Flags Over Adam Silver’s Plan To Test Microchip-Embedded Basketballs
articles.summary: NBA Commissioner Adam Silver has revealed that the league is developing a basketball with a tiny embedded chip that could help officials make calls more accu...
articles.body:
NBA Commissioner Adam Silver has revealed that the league is developing a basketball with a tiny embedded chip that could help officials make calls more accurately.

While the technology is meant to improve officiating, the announcement sparked suspicion among fans, who raised concerns about the possibility of a "magnet ball."

Adam Silver's Explanation of NBA's 'Smart' Basketball Raises Alarm

Speaking during a Sunday preseason appearance, Silver explained that the NBA is working with Wilson on a "smart ball" that contains a chip weighing roughly 1 gram.

He noted that a standard basketball weighs around 620 grams, and the league has tested the technology in the NBA G League and Summer League without players noticing a difference.

Silver believes the chip could help referees determine whether a player touched the ball before it went out of bounds by tracking changes in its spin. It could also provide information about a shot's arc and eventually help young players understand their shooting technique.

"We think it's an opportunity where, by any change in the spin of the ball, you can tell, for example, if a finger touched the ball and it was going out of bounds," Silver explained .

"For [goaltending], you can tell if the arc changed in the shot. I think there's also gonna be other applications, ultimately for consumers."

Silver added that the technology could be used for officiating "as soon as next year."

Still, NBA fans remain wary, with some drawing comparisons to the conspiracy theory often called "magnet ball." The theory alleges that technology can influence the ball's movement to produce a desired result.

Although there is no evidence that the NBA's proposed chip is designed to manipulate games, one fan was quick to bring up the nickname, writing , "AKA magnet ball, they not even tryna hide it."

Another made a similar joke about the league's plans, saying , "Magnet ball 2.0 incoming."

Some weren't convinced the technology was necessary. One frustrated fan simply asked , "Why, man, why?"

Another reaction highlighted how unbelievable the announcement sounded: "Magnet ball will actually be a real thing."

One more user questioned the need for the change altogether, writing , "Bro adding [expletive] for what?"

The backlash reflects a wider lack of trust among a portion of fans who already question referees' decision-making and worry that new technology could create more room for controversy. Still, Silver has presented the chip as a tool for improving accuracy, not manipulating results.

Notably, the idea of using technology to help officials is not new. The official ball at the 2026 FIFA World Cup featured a connected sensor that sent real-time data to video officials and helped them identify ball contact and make decisions more quickly.

With the NBA regular season set to begin on Oct. 20, the smart ball is not yet part of regular-season officiating. For now, the league is testing whether it can make the game easier to judge. Whether fans will ever trust the technology is another question entirely.

articles.title: Nikola Jokic envía un mensaje a sus críticos con un triple-doble
articles.standfirst: El serbio lideró la victoria de su equipo ante los Bulls con 20 puntos, 11 rebotes y 10 asistencias
articles.summary: El serbio lideró la victoria de su equipo ante los Bulls con
articles.body: Recientemente algunos críticos señalaban que el problema de Nikola Jokic es que ve el baloncesto como una profesión más, que no tiene pasión por jugar. Pero es que la imagen que da en pista puede engañar. Al menos, él mismo ha reconocido que "amo el baloncesto". Para responder a los críticos, nada mejor que hechos. En un partido de pretemporada, sin más misión que la de obtener rodaje, Jokic hizo lo que mejor sabe hacer en pista: un triple-doble. Lo firmó en tres cuartos, exactamente en 26 minutos de juego, logrando 22 puntos, 11 rebotes y 10 asistencias. Hizo un 8/12 en tiros de campo, con 1/2 en triples. Pero no sólo fue lo que hizo en pista, sino lo que hizo cuando estaba en el banquillo. Se fue del choque al final del tercer cuarto y ya no volvió. En ese momento su equipo ganaba 99-94 gracias a una última canasta de Alpha Diallo. Durante el cuarto periodo se pudo ver a Jokic levantándose en todo momento, haciendo indicaciones a los más jóvenes, pidiendo más defensa, más orden o que se hiciera bien alguna jugada. Luego, al final del partido, explicó su actitud: "Quiero ganar el partido siempre. Amo el baloncesto. Creo que cada detalle cuenta, especialmente cuando están los más jóvenes en la pista. Es bueno ver cómo aprenden y progresan, lo disfruto". Ni su actitud ni sus palabras parecen de alguien que crea que el baloncesto es sólo una profesión. Jokic tendrá que liderar a los Nuggets en un nuevo intento por recuperar su trono en el Oeste. No será ffácil. En principio los Nuggets parten en un escalón inferior a la hora de hablar de candidatos, por debajo de los Thunder y de los Spurs. Manejar la vetarnía de jugadores como Murray, DeRozan o Gordon con la juventud pujante de otros como Whitmore o Miller será una de las claves a lo largo de la temporada de los de Colorado.

articles.title: El balón inteligente que prepara la NBA
articles.standfirst: Adam Silver reconoció que ya se han hecho pruebas y que podría incluirse esta misma temporada
articles.summary: Adam Silver reconoció que ya se han hecho pruebas y que podría incluirse esta misma temporada
articles.body: Adam Silver sorprendió este pasado domingo en un partido de pretemporada al revelar en los micrófonos de la NBC que la NBA estaba trabajando en un balón inteligente. El Comisionado explicó que se trataba de un experimento, pero que su inclusión podría estar tan cercana como en esta misma temporada pero ya en el año 2027. Silver dejó claro que la nueva tecnología que iría implantada en cada balón servirá para mejorar la rapidez y exactitud de ciertas decisiones arbitrales, como un fuera de banda o el goaltending, es decir, interferir en el tiro cuando el balón esta bajando o si este está sobre el círculo del aro. Además, también podría servir para mejorar el tiro de un jugador porque analiza las trayectorias y las parábolas. La tecnología consiste en la inclusión en el balón de un chip inteligente de apenas un gramo de peso, lo que no tiene que afectar al peso del balón que es de 620 gramos. De hecho, Silver confirmó que se han hecho pruebas en partidos de la G League, de la Liga de verano e incluso de pretemporada sin recibir ninguna queja de los jugadores, incluso veteranos, sobre el peso del balón. Nadie notó la diferencia. "Creemos que es una oportunidad en la que, por cualquier cambio en el giro de la pelota, se puede saber, por ejemplo, si un dedo tocó la pelota y esta iba a salir fuera", decía Silver. "En el caso de la interferencia con el tiro (goaltending), se puede apreciar si la trayectoria del lanzamiento cambió. Creo que también habrá otras aplicaciones, en última instancia para los consumidores, como la salida del balón de la mano o el arco que se da a un tiro". No ha faltado la típica teoría de la conspiración en las redes sociales que en este caso se llama: 'El balón magnético', que habla de que ese chip puede influir en los tiros para lograr el resultado deseado. Es decir, la manipulación de los partidos. Será un tema recurrente en las redes. En cualquier caso no es una tecnología nueva. En fútbol, la FIFA introdujo durante el Mundial 2026 para saber si un balón entraba o no por completo en la portería. Esa tecnología ya está instaurada en las grandes competiciones.

articles.title: Cooper Flagg Says Mavs Teammates 'Definitely Try' to Treat Him Like a Rookie Still, Kyrie Hypes Star
articles.summary: Entering his second season in the NBA, reigning Rookie of the Year Cooper Flagg is still being treated like a first-year pro by his veteran Dallas Mavericks teammates.
articles.body:
Entering his second season in the NBA, reigning Rookie of the Year Cooper Flagg is still being treated like a first-year pro by his veteran Dallas Mavericks teammates.

Flagg told ESPN's Brian Windhorst that he was still tasked with "various menial duties," such as carrying bags, during the team's preseason trip to China. After all, the 2025 No. 1 overall pick is still technically a rookie until his sophomore season officially begins later this month.

"I can sometimes sneak by without them remembering that they want me to be a rookie still. But yeah, they definitely try," Flagg said.

Despite the good-natured ribbing from his older teammates, Flagg appears ready to ascend even further in his second year in the league. In two preseason games against the Houston Rockets, the 19-year-old recorded 33 points, 10 rebounds, 10 assists, three steals and two blocks across 45 minutes of action.

"He's going to lead this franchise into the future. You can definitely bank on that," Mavs star point guard Kyrie Irving said. "He deserves a lot of the praise he's gotten because he's carried a lot. … He's wise beyond his years."

Flagg is the new face of a franchise that is still rebuilding after trading star point guard Luka Doncic to the Los Angeles Lakers in 2025. The youngster said that he's prepared to step up as a leader this year as the Mavs try to keep pace in the competitive Western Conference.

"I'm just finding my voice," Flagg said. "Being so young and a little bit inexperienced is tough sometimes, but I think up to this point, I've earned the respect of my teammates, and I've gotten that sense that they really respect me and my opinion."

Flagg and the Mavs will open the 2026-27 season on Oct. 21 against the Rockets.

articles.title: Michael Jordan jersey from 1998 NBA Finals sells for $14 million
articles.summary: Michael Jordan memorabilia from the 1998 NBA Finals tends to fetch a high price.
articles.body:
The 1997-98 NBA season was Michael Jordan's "Last Dance" with the Chicago Bulls. By now, everyone knows the story. Jordan and Co. entered the year knowing it would be the last time the team's current roster would be together. Because of that, it was championship or bust for the Bulls.

Sure enough, Jordan willed his team to another title. Thanks to a fantastic showing in the 1998 NBA Finals, in which Jordan won the Finals MVP award after averaging 33.5 points per game, the Bulls pulled off the feat, securing the team's second three-peat. With that task complete, Jordan retired from the NBA for the second time in his career.

All of those factors likely led to one of Jordan's game-worn jerseys from those Finals going for an astounding $14 million at an auction. Hunt Auctions in Pennsylvania announced Monday that the jersey Jordan wore in Game 2 of the 1998 NBA Finals sold to a Miami real estate investor for that price.

The figure is — perhaps surprisingly — not a record . That belongs to a game-worn Babe Ruth jersey, per the Associated Press. That jersey, which sold for $24.12 million in 2024, was the one worn by Ruth when he hit his "called shot" home run.

Perhaps unsurprisingly, Jordan memorabilia from the 1998 NBA Finals tends to draw significant interest at auctions. Jordan's Game 2 jersey is the third from that particular Finals to bring in over $10 million during an auction.

A signed Michael Jordan Chicago Bulls jersey was sold at an auction for a reported record-setting price.

Per Tim Reynolds of the Associated Press, Pennsylvania-based Hunt Auctions announced that a game-worn, autographed Jordan road jersey from the 1998 NBA Finals was privately sold for $14 million, marking the "highest price ever paid for a piece of basketball memorabilia."

Miami real estate investor Ron Firman was identified as the buyer, and he owns multiple rare collector's items:

Jordan wore the jersey in Game 2 against the Utah Jazz and dropped 37 points to help the Bulls tie the series 1-1. Chicago eventually won the NBA Finals in six games, giving Jordan his sixth championship ring. The 1997-98 season later became the subject of the iconic 10-episode Last Dance documentary series, which was released in 2020.

"While Michael Jordan's importance within the sports memorabilia marketplace has long been established it has now escalated to an elite asset class more typically reserved for iconic works of art," David Hunt, president of Hunt Auctions, said. "We are very pleased to have been able to facilitate this historic sale which serves as another benchmark for our industry."

Jordan's 1998 NBA Finals memorabilia is among the most lucrative sources in the collector space. Reynolds noted that his Game 1 jersey was sold at auction for about $10.1 million in 2022, and his jersey from Game 3 was auctioned last month for nearly $12.3 million. In 2023, a pair of Air Jordan sneakers worn in Game 2 was sold by Sotheby's for $2.2 million, which at the time was deemed "a new world record for the most valuable sneakers ever sold."

Reynolds added, "The $14 million price would be the second-biggest known cost for a game-worn jersey, behind the $24.12 million paid in 2024 for the jersey worn by Babe Ruth of the New York Yankees when he hit the 'called shot' home run against the Chicago Cubs at Wrigley Field in Game 3 of the 1932 World Series."

"Michael Jordan was an incredibly talented player who is admired around the world," Firman said in a release. "I'm very excited about the purchase."

articles.title: 2026-27 Fantasy Basketball All-Breakout Team: 6 players who will take a step forward this season
articles.summary: Here's a look at Dan Titus' top breakout candidates for fantasy basketball at each position in 2026-27.
articles.body:
Every fantasy basketball season presents an opportunity to find the next group of players ready to break out. Whether it's second-year guys on the verge of earning a bigger role, an unproven talent looking to establish himself, or a late-round sleeper with untapped potential, these are the players who could emerge as valuable fantasy assets in the 2026-27 season.

For other breakout candidates I'm targeting along with my favorite picks, projections, position previews, strategies and 100 players profiles, subscribe to Fantasy Ultra to unlock 50+ page basketball Draft Playbook ! Below is a glimpse of what the full Draft Playbook has to offer.

2026-27 Fantasy Basketball All-Breakout Team

Guard — Brandin Podziemski, Warriors (Yahoo ADP: 116.5)

Podziemski already does some things I love from a fantasy guard, particularly rebounding and secondary playmaking. Now, I want to see what happens if the offensive volume increases. The Warriors notably struck out on most prominent free agents and did nothing to fortify their backcourt alongside Stephen Curry. So, it's a chance for Podz to prove his worth. Golden State clearly believes he's ready, signing Podziemski to a five-year, $110 million extension .

Guard — Dylan Harper, Spurs (Yahoo ADP: 82.2)

Harper is talented enough that I'm willing to live with the crowded backcourt. The question isn't whether he'll start, it's whether his minutes will rise after an impressive rookie year and playoff run that ended in the NBA Finals. I think they will; with his size, expect the Spurs to tinker with more three-guard sets to ensure their best players are on the floor, especially in crunch time. There is some real potential as a stat-stuffer across categories and I'm projecting Harper to score 46.1 FPPG in High Score. Sometimes the simplest breakout case is just betting on talent. Anyone with eyes sees he's got that "it" factor.

Forward — Brandon Miller, Hornets (Yahoo ADP: 44.6)

LaMelo Ball's departure opens the door for Miller to become Charlotte's primary scorer, and that's the breakout I'm betting on. He's already shown he can handle significant shot volume and be a high-end source of 3s, but now there's an opportunity to take another step as a playmaker and rebounder while moving to the top of the offensive hierarchy. The biggest concern for 9-cat remains FG%, especially if the shot attempts spike. But entering Year 4 with the green light to lead this offense, Miller has the setup to put together his best fantasy season yet.

Forward — Ausar Thompson, Pistons (Yahoo ADP: 82.6)

Detroit signed Thompson to a lucrative extension without making any major additions to the starting lineup, so the money says they're banking on an offensive leap. He's arguably already one of the best perimeter defenders in the game, and the rebounds, stocks and low-key assists give him a strong fantasy base. The most he's averaged is 26 minutes per game, so imagine what happens if that number pushes into the 30s. The hype train has already left the station and it'll likely cost a mid-round pick to get him, but any meaningful growth as a scorer could be enough for Thompson to meet his rising ADP. He's going to do numbers if the minutes finally match the talent.

Center — Day'Ron Sharpe, Nets (Yahoo ADP: 93.8)

Nic Claxton's departure finally gives Sharpe the opportunity fantasy managers have been waiting for. The rebounding and steals have always popped on a per-minute basis, and now Brooklyn can give him the runway to prove those numbers translate as a starter. He's also shown enough touch around the basket and passing ability to offer more than boards alone. There's some risk in paying for production we haven't seen over a full season, but this is the clearest path Sharpe has had to becoming a legitimate standard-league center.

UTIL — Matas Buzelis, Bulls (Yahoo ADP: 64.9)

Buzelis is climbing draft boards, and it's easy to understand why. He could legitimately challenge Norman Powell as Chicago's leading scorer while also bringing the rebounds, 3s and stocks that make his fantasy profile so appealing. He played 77 games last season and established career bests across nearly every category outside of FT% and turnovers, giving us more than just projection to work with entering Year 3. Fantasy analysts are expecting the next step, and I'm there with them. The draft price is rising, but so is the ceiling.

The clock is ticking for Payton Pritchard and the Boston Celtics .

On Oct. 1, Pritchard became eligible for a three-year, $69 million extension. Nearly two weeks later, the two sides have yet to reach an agreement.

And with a deadline approaching, the window for Pritchard and the Celtics to sign an extension is closing.

When is Payton Pritchard's extension deadline?

Pritchard has until Oct. 19 to sign an extension with the Celtics, one day before the 2026-27 NBA regular season begins.

Pritchard is under contract through 2027-28. If the two sides don't reach an agreement by Oct. 19, they can revisit contract negotiations in July 2027.

The most Pritchard can sign for this summer is a three-year, $69 million extension. If he waits until next offseason, he could be eligible for a four-year, roughly $100 million extension.

Pritchard has made a strong case for a significant raise. He won the NBA's Sixth Man of the Year award in 2024-25 before averaging career highs of 17.0 points, 5.2 assists and 3.9 rebounds in 2025-26. He started 50 of 79 games last season.

If Pritchard takes another step forward this season, his value could rise even further.

That gives Pritchard and the Celtics plenty to consider before the Oct. 19 deadline.

Pritchard signed a four-year, $30 million extension with the Celtics in 2023.

articles.title: The unsung Brewers rookie hero who somehow got better of Tarik Skubal to beat Dodgers in NLCS Game 1
articles.summary: The Milwaukee Brewers opened the National League Championship Series with a 2-1 win over the Los Angeles Dodgers on Sunday at American Family Field. While ri...
articles.body:
The Milwaukee Brewers opened the National League Championship Series with a 2-1 win over the Los Angeles Dodgers on Sunday at American Family Field. While rising star Brice Turang's home run helped Milwaukee get on the scoreboard , it was rookie Luis Lara who came through in the clutch against Tarik Skubal , the two-time reigning American League Cy Young Award winner.

Making his first NLCS start, the 21-year-old drove in the go-ahead run in the fifth inning, helping the Brewers draw first blood over the defending World Series champions.

Lara entered Game 1 with just 61 games of major-league experience after making his debut in early July. He had recorded a .246/.311/.325 batting line during his first season in the majors, but Milwaukee trusted him to start in right field with Skubal on the mound, because of his switch-hitting ability.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The outfielders first plate appearance offered little indication of what was coming. Batting eighth, Lara struck out against a 97.6 mph sinker above the strike zone after seeing four pitches from the veteran southpaw.

However, his next opportunity was where the game turned on its head.

Garrett Mitchell opened the bottom of the fifth with a four-pitch walk before fellow rookie Cooper Pratt advanced him to second with a sacrifice bunt. Lara then attacked the first pitch he saw, sending Skubal's changeup up the middle into center field. Mitchell scored without a throw, giving Milwaukee a 2-1 advantage that it maintained through the final out.

Skubal exited after five innings, allowing two runs on five hits while striking out seven and walking two. A 25-pitch fifth inning contributed to his early departure.

Lara's breakthrough came after an impressive run at Triple-A Nashville, where he compiled a .321/.432/.470 slash line across his first 78 games. His progress at the plate, combined with his defensive ability, helped earn him a seven-year, $31 million contract during the season. He had also won a minor-league Gold Glove the previous year.

The Brewers once again relied on their steady bullpen after starter Jacob Misiorowski couldn't make it through five innings. The right-hander surrendered five hits and three walks while striking out five over 4⅓ innings. Shohei Ohtani scored in the second on an Andy Pages single, but Milwaukee prevented further damage with an inning-ending double play after Los Angeles loaded the bases.

The Brewers' bullpen subsequently pitched 4⅔ scoreless innings, allowing just two hits. Aaron Ashby contributed two innings and extended his scoreless postseason stretch to 7⅔ innings.

Trevor Megill earned the save despite walking Kyle Tucker and pinch-hitter Josue De Paula with two outs in the ninth. He finished the game by inducing a deep fly ball from Mookie Betts that was caught near the center-field warning track.

Milwaukee has more reason to celebrate after being swept by the Dodgers in last year's NLCS without ever leading in a single inning. The Brewers are now seeking their first World Series appearance since 1982.

London briefly threatened to make a contest of it towards the end of the first quarter.

Ethan Price hit two three-pointers from 26 feet in the space of 40 seconds, both assisted by Devante Adams either side of a Deni Avdija layup, to bring the Lions within four points at 23-19 with three minutes remaining in the period.

But Portland took control with a 38-12 second quarter, including a 15-0 run over the final four minutes of the half.

Maxwell Lewis, the only London player with previous NBA experience, led the Lions with 13 points, five rebounds and a game-high four steals.

Adams added 12 points off the bench, while Price and Joel Scott contributed eight apiece. Six of Scott's points came in the fourth quarter, while Thomas Kennedy collected six rebounds, including three offensive boards.

Great Britain international Tarik Phillip endured a difficult night, missing all eight of his field-goal attempts, including five from three-point range. His three points came entirely from the free-throw line.

Portland's five starters played a combined 76 minutes for 45 points. None of them appeared after half-time.

Toumani Camara and Scoot Henderson led the Trail Blazers with 14 points each. Henderson made four of his five three-point attempts in just 16 minutes off the bench.

Yang Hansen added 13 points and four assists, including a three-pointer from 25 feet, while Sidy Cissoko also scored 13, shooting a perfect 5 of 5 from the field and making all three of his attempts from beyond the arc.

Jeremy Sochan, who grew up in England, finished with eight points and a game-high eight rebounds, while marquee name Ja Morant scored five points and dished five dimes.

Deni Avdija recorded a game-best plus-minus of +44 in 17 minutes, while London's Keenan Evans finished at -45 in 20 minutes.

Damian Lillard, Robert Williams III, Shaedon Sharpe and Chris Youngblood did not feature for the Trail Blazers.

Coach Sabonis returns to where his father made his name

London are coached by Tautvydas Sabonis, whose father Arvydas spent seven seasons with Portland across the 1990s and early 2000s. Tautvydas had not visited the city for more than a decade.

Sabonis admitted the timing of the trip was far from ideal.

"If I had to choose a different timing, I would definitely choose it in the preseason, not now," he said.

Last season was his first in charge of the Lions, who won all four domestic competitions.

London are the reigning Super League Basketball champions, have started this season 5-0 in the SLB and have won one of their opening two EuroCup group games. In 2024, they became the first British men's club to reach the EuroCup semi-finals.

The Lions made a round trip of almost 10,000 miles in the middle of their domestic and European campaigns, arriving in Portland on Saturday afternoon before departing immediately after the game. They host Skyliners Frankfurt in the EuroCup on Thursday.

To minimise jet lag, the squad remained on British time throughout their stay in Oregon, waking at around 4am for breakfast.

A historic meeting with implications beyond Portland

The closest British and NBA club basketball had previously come to such a meeting was the 1995 McDonald's Championship, when Sheffield Sharks and Houston Rockets participated in the same tournament but did not face each other.

The Lions have submitted a bid to join the EuroLeague, which has ambitions to expand from 20 to 24 clubs by the 2027-28 season.

Owned by Lithuanian technology company Tesonet, London also became the first British basketball club to wear Jordan Brand kit this season.

Meanwhile, the proposed NBA Europe competition has placed renewed attention on the British market, with London and Manchester both discussed as potential franchise cities.

Monday's exhibition was not connected to that project, but it offered the Lions an opportunity to test themselves against NBA opposition and put British club basketball on an international stage.

The result demonstrated the gulf between the teams. The occasion, however, was about more than the scoreline.

articles.title: Why Roddy Gayle Jr. didn't play in Michigan basketball exhibition
articles.summary: Roddy Gayle Jr. was in Ann Arbor, but didn't play in a Michigan basketball exhibition win over EMU. Coach Mike Boynton Jr. explained why Monday.
articles.body:
After an offseason of wondering if Roddy Gayle Jr. had another season of Michigan basketball eligibility, he was on hand for the Wolverines' 87-62 exhibition win over Eastern Michigan.

Just one problem, though: He never took off his warmup outfit, spending his entire afternoon on Sunday, Oct. 11, on the Crisler Center bench. The reason? Some suspect wording on last month's New York court ruling ostensibly giving him a fifth year of NCAA participation.

"All this stuff is fairly nuanced," coach Mike Boynton Jr. said while explaining why Kenny Noland, a transfer from Columbia who also won a fifth year through the courts, was cleared to play but Gayle was not. "His injunction order didn't address his participation in [NBA] Summer League. Simple as that.

"There needs to be an amendment added to the injunction that says, 'This includes not having anything to do with his participation in Summer League,' which we hope will be in the next couple days."

The hope for Gayle, who spent a couple weeks on the Detroit Pistons' Las Vegas Summer League squad but did not sign an Exhibit 10 contract, is to be able to play in U-M's next exhibition, against Oregon State (led by former Michigan assistant Justin Joyner) on Friday (7 p.m., B1G+).

Gayle is one of dozens of players across the country who took the NCAA to court to gain eligibility under its adopted-in-June "five-in-five" rule, which states players may play five years of college athletics beginning immediately after high school or they turn 19, whichever comes first.

Still, even without court time, Gayle has been a vocal leader during practice and a stabilizing force on the bench, according to teammate J.P. Estrella.

"It's great having that veteran leader back," the Tennessee transfer said after he scored 14 points Sunday. "He's a guy that made a huge impact last year, and he's already making a huge impact already this year in practice. Just talking, just telling us little things, even on the bench today in the huddles.

"He really has a big voice in this group, which is super beneficial because we need that out of him − just his overall game is really good. I mean, we're gonna be really good if we get him [back and] get this thing rolling."

Gayle played in 39 of U-M's 40 games last season, averaging 7.3 points, 3.3 rebounds and 1.3 assists in 21.1 minutes per game. He played in 146 games across his career, starting 72 games (including 25 for U-M in 2025-26).

Michigan is thin on the wing after freshman Brandon McCoy Jr. was lost for the season to an ACL injury. Without the McDonald's All-American or Gayle, the Wolverines would be relying on a combination of Ricky Liburd (who redshirted last year), Oscar Goodman (who more naturally fits as a four) and freshmen Quinn Costello, Malachi Brown and Joseph Hartmann.

Even with the uncertainty, Michigan is working as though it will have Gayle for a third season in Ann Arbor (after he spent his first two years with Ohio State).

"There's a there's an aspect of of this that's new for everybody, right?," Boynton said last week at the Big Ten's basketball media days. "This is sort of uncharted territory. Right now, he's eligible. We're functioning as if he's eligible. ... We feel like he's got a strong case. We're excited about the opportunity and the things that he adds to our team, and we look forward to moving forward with the information we have in front of us."

Tony Garcia is the Michigan beat writer for the Detroit Free Press. Email him at apgarcia@freepress.com and follow him on X at @RealTonyGarcia .
